note: Independent reviewer, 12 stills (8 rooms, a shop, 3 fight frames), target Hollow Knight. Biggest lever: one character and foe art pass (matching hero, real boss creatures). Caveat: the 'beige hero' defect in the fight frames is the Barkbalm sheen the capture turned on, not the hero's normal look. The loop's own rubric for pass 492 is 96.8/100.
defects: Image 08 (Evercrown heart gate): cyan crystal spikes read as stamped over the foes and hide their silhouettes.
The Haar Wyrm reads as placeholder geometry: flat green circles with box heads on chains of discs.
Fight frames: the hero looks washed out next to exploration shots (partly the capture's Barkbalm sheen).
High Boughs: smooth high-resolution branches behind chunky pixel tiles look like two games layered.
The same domed hut repeats across biomes, and town rooms are flat corridors with townsfolk in a row.
Noisy checkerboard brick ceilings and floors frame every room in the same heavy rectangle.
Gnarlmaw's title card is faint and low-contrast.
Characters are about 30 px tall on a 540 px frame with little presence against large empty backdrops.

note: Independent reviewer, 12 stills (9 zone rooms, a shop, 2 guardians), target Hollow Knight, no hints. Up from 4.1 at pass 492. Reads as mid-tier indie, not hand-crafted: flat tile grids, flat lighting, a hero sprite far below the environment's fidelity. Fastest wins named: upgrade the player sprite, add contact shadows/AO where platforms meet walls, tile variants plus stronger atmospheric-perspective depth between the play layer and parallax. The loop's own rubric for pass 497 is 96.9/100.
defects: Player character fidelity gap: the hero is a small, soft, low-detail hooded figure with no readable silhouette or gear detail, far below the environment art.
Flat lighting with no ambient occlusion: walls meet floors and platforms meet backgrounds with hard, unshaded seams; light sources rarely cast gradient pools or contact shadows.
Visible tile repetition and grid banding: brick and wall fields tile obviously, with little tile variation, damage, or hand-placed detail to break the grid.
Foreground and background collapse to the same depth plane: trunks, mid platforms and the play layer share similar value and saturation, so the player can get lost against busy backdrops.
Boxy, framed rooms with dead space: many rooms are rectangles bounded by a thick wall border with large empty centers.
Over-reliance on halftone/dot-screen gradient fills standing in for real rendering, flattening large areas.
Generic, undersized foes with weak silhouettes.
Platforms are one uniform stamped plank sprite repeated across every biome.
